QueryMinLedger.name: minLedger
QueryMinLedger.summary: first ledger of the range, inclusive
QueryMinLedger.description: The first ledger in the range (inclusive). Required for ascending scans (`order: asc`) and optional for descending scans. Specify this parameter only when starting a query, not when continuing with a cursor.

QueryMaxLedger.name: maxLedger
QueryMaxLedger.summary: last ledger of the range, inclusive
QueryMaxLedger.description: The last ledger in the range (inclusive). Optional. Without `maxLedger`, an ascending scan continues toward newly closed ledgers and reports `WAITING_FOR_LEDGERS` when it catches up to the chain. A descending scan starts at the latest ledger. Specify this parameter only when starting a query.

QueryOrder.name: order
QueryOrder.description: The direction of the scan. `asc` (default) scans forward from `minLedger`; `desc` scans backward from `maxLedger`. Specify this parameter only when starting a query.

QueryEventFilters.name: filters
QueryEventFilters.summary: list of filters; AND inside a filter, OR across filters
QueryEventFilters.description:
An array of 1 to 256 event filters. An event matches if it satisfies at least one filter; within a filter, all specified fields must match. Omit `filters` to match all events. Specify this parameter only when starting a query.

For example, to match either `transfer` or `mint` events from one contract, send two filters with the same `contractId` and a different `topic0`. The first example below does this.

Topic values are Base64-encoded XDR `ScVal`s, not plain strings. Use the [JSON to XDR](https://lab.stellar.org/xdr/to) page in the Lab to encode a value.

A query may use at most 15 distinct index terms by default; node operators can configure this limit. Each distinct `contractId` is one term, each distinct `type` is one term, and each distinct value at a given topic position is one term. The same value at the same position counts once no matter how many filters repeat it. The same value at two different positions counts twice. For example, `[{ topic0: transfer, topic1: me }, { topic0: transfer, topic2: me }]` uses 3 terms. A query over the budget returns `invalid_params` with `termsUsed` and `termBudget` in `error.data`.

QueryCursor.name: cursor
QueryCursor.description: The cursor returned by the previous response, used to continue a query. It preserves the ledger bounds, scan order, and filters. Do not combine `cursor` with `minLedger`, `maxLedger`, `order`, or `filters`; doing so returns an error.

QueryLimit.name: limit
QueryLimit.description: The maximum number of events to return per page, from 1 to 1,000. Defaults to 100. This setting is not stored in the cursor; include it on each request to retain a nondefault value.

QueryFormat.name: xdrFormat
QueryFormat.summary: chooses a response format for XDR fields: 'json' or 'base64'
QueryFormat.description: Controls how XDR values are represented in the response: decoded JSON or Base64-encoded XDR. Do not depend on a fixed schema for the JSON representation, as it may change with the underlying XDR.
